note:
Anticipated returns, as distinct from delivered ones.

Everything else in this app is backward-looking: expected goals per 90 describes chances a player has already had, form describes points already scored. Both share a blind spot -- they don't know what a manager said yesterday, that a defence is missing two centre-backs, or that this striker has scored in four straight against this opponent.

`anytime_goalscorer` is the decimal price. Implied probability is the raw 1/odds figure, which includes the bookmaker's margin and so runs a few points high; that overround is left in deliberately, because removing it needs the full market for the fixture and a fabricated correction is worse than a known bias.

`captain_share` is the percentage of managers expected to captain the player. It is the single most important number for rank and appears nowhere in the FPL API, so it is researched here. Ownership plus captain share is effective ownership: if 60% of the field captains someone, his haul barely moves your rank and his blank barely hurts it.

`matchups` is what typically happens when these sides meet -- the thing a per-90 rate cannot express and every human analyst reaches for first.

Prices move. The research date above is the honest shelf life of this file.

players.note: Included to make the point: even the best-scoring defender in FPL history is a 9/1 shot to score. That is what a defender's captaincy ceiling actually looks like.
